pt6_rw_m2_q13:
Table: baseline precipitation (somewhat concentrated / evenly distributed) vs % change in aquifer input, surface irrigation, groundwater irrigation. Persad et al. concluded concentrating precipitation triggers more irrigation, but the change is highly sensitive to baseline concentration.

Which choice best describes data from the table that support Persad and colleagues' conclusion?

Persad and colleagues modeled what happens to irrigation when a region's yearly precipitation becomes concentrated into fewer, heavier events. Where the baseline precipitation was already somewhat concentrated, the model showed aquifer input rising 4.9%, surface irrigation rising 0.4%, and groundwater irrigation rising 0.9%. Where the baseline precipitation had been evenly distributed, surface irrigation rose 9.0% and groundwater irrigation rose 7.9%. The researchers concluded that concentrating precipitation triggers more irrigation, but that the size of the change is highly sensitive to how concentrated the baseline precipitation already was.

Which choice best describes data that support Persad and colleagues' conclusion?
pt8_rw_m2_q12:
Graph: type A flies (DptA silenced) stay near 90% survival after A. sicerae infection; type B and type AB flies (DptB silenced, alone or with DptA) drop to near 0%. Text also states DptA activity — not DptB — correlates with resistance to a different bacterium, P. rettgeri.

Which choice most logically completes the statement about what the data in the graph suggest?

In an experiment, flies whose DptA gene was silenced (type A) stayed near 90% survival after infection with A. sicerae, while flies whose DptB gene was silenced — alone (type B) or together with DptA (type AB) — dropped to near 0% survival. Separately, it is DptA activity, not DptB, that correlates with resistance to a different bacterium, P. rettgeri.

Which choice most logically completes the statement about what these data suggest?
